- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.  
- If model shows strong mean reversion bias (e.g., forecast drops sharply after rising), check if sentiment is weakening — if so, adjust downward slightly to reflect reduced momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent trends; if sentiment is neutral or mixed, reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.3 → -0.3 → +0.3), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment shift.
